footer.privacy: IntuneAppFastDeploy {version} — no telemetry: this tool only talks to Microsoft and to the links you give it.
setup.title: Configuration needed
setup.text: TENANT_ID and CLIENT_ID are not set. Create the app registration in Microsoft Entra ID as described in the README, put both values in docker-compose.yml, then run: docker compose up -d
login.title: Sign in
login.text: Sign in with your Intune administrator account. The tool acts with your own rights and stores no password.
apps.title: Windows applications (Win32)
apps.empty: No Win32 application in Intune yet.
apps.name: Name
app.superseded_by: This is an old version: it is replaced by {name}.
rollout.title: Pilot and production groups
rollout.text: These groups are saved on this server (config/rollout.json), not in Intune, and follow the application from one version to the next. What Intune applies today is on the “Assignments” line above.
rollout.text_new: Who receives this application. These groups are saved on this server (config/rollout.json), not in Intune, and are used again for the next versions.
rollout.save_hint: **Save groups** keeps these settings for the next publication and for **Go to production**. Nothing changes in Intune yet.
rollout.promote_hint: **Go to production** adds the production groups to this version in Intune, now. The pilot groups keep it. Save first if you have just changed the groups.
rollout.pilot_hint: The groups that receive a new version first, to try it. Used when you publish with “The pilot groups first”.
rollout.prod_hint: The groups that receive it next: added when you click “Go to production”, or at once when you publish with “Production directly”. If empty, the assignments of the previous version are reused.
rollout.prod_hint_new: The groups that receive it next: added when you click “Go to production”, or at once when you publish with “Production directly”.
rollout.manual: Or enter an Object ID by hand
groups.search_hint: Searches Microsoft Entra ID by the start of the name and shows 20 groups at most. Click a group to add it.
groups.search_teaser: A group can be chosen by searching its name in Microsoft Entra ID, without copying its Object ID. This search is an option, turned off on this installation.
groups.setup_show: How to enable the search by name
groups.setup_intro: Done once, by someone who can grant admin consent in Microsoft Entra ID. It takes about five minutes.
groups.setup_step1: Open the Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com) and go to **Identity → Applications → App registrations**, then open the registration this tool uses.
groups.setup_step2: **API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions**: search for `GroupMember.Read.All`, tick it and click **Add permissions**.
groups.setup_step3: Click **Grant admin consent for <your organization>** and confirm. The status column must show a green tick next to `GroupMember.Read.All`.
groups.setup_step4: Only then, on the server, in `docker-compose.yml`: replace `ENABLE_GROUP_PICKER: "false"` with `ENABLE_GROUP_PICKER: "true"`.
groups.setup_step5: Restart the tool with `docker compose up -d`, reload this page and sign in again.
groups.setup_order: Keep this order. If the setting is turned on before the consent is granted, signing in to the tool fails. To go back: set it to `"false"` again and run `docker compose up -d`.
groups.setup_scope: `GroupMember.Read.All` gives read-only access to groups and their members, with the rights of the signed-in person. The tool only uses it for this search.
groups.label_hint: The label is a reminder for you: it is shown here instead of the identifier and stays on this server. It is not sent to Intune.
groups.find_id_show: Where to find the Object ID of a group
groups.find_id_text: In the Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com): **Groups → All groups**, open the group, then **Overview → Object ID**. Copy the value (36 characters, like `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`) and paste it here.
groups.all_devices_hint: **All devices**: every device enrolled in Intune.
groups.all_users_hint: **All users**: every user of your organization. Neither needs a group to be created or kept up to date.
groups.intent_required_hint: **Required**: Intune installs the application by itself on the devices of these targets.
groups.intent_available_hint: **Available**: the application is offered in the Company Portal and each person installs it if they want.
rollout.confirm_promote: Assign “{name}” to the production groups now?
rollout.to_pilot_hint: Only the pilot groups receive it. When the trial is conclusive, **Go to production**, on the application page, adds the production groups.
rollout.to_prod_hint: The production groups, and the pilot groups if there are any, receive it as soon as it is published, with no trial phase.
rollout.to_prod_previous: With no production group configured, the assignments of the previous version are reused.
rollout.to_none_hint: It is created in Intune with no assignment: no device receives it until you assign it in the Intune portal.
rollout.no_pilot_hint: No pilot group is configured for this application: set them on its page to enable the pilot phase.
notify.label: Notifications to users
notify.hint: What people see on their device when Intune installs this application. Used for the assignments this tool creates from now on (pilot, production, going to production); assignments that already exist in Intune are not changed.
notify.show_all_hint: On the device: the usual Intune messages (download, installation, restart).
notify.show_reboot_hint: On the device: nothing, except when a restart is needed.
wizard.link: Download link of the installer (MSI or EXE)
wizard.link_hint: The file is downloaded by the server, analyzed, and nothing is sent to Intune before you confirm.
wizard.file: Or choose a file from this computer
step.supersede: Declaring the replacement of the previous version
review.title: Check before publishing
form.install_unknown: Installer type not recognized: add the silent switch yourself (often /S, /silent or /quiet).
form.uninstall_hint: Cannot be read from the file. Usual form for this installer: {example}
form.run_as_update_hint: Taken from the current application. Change it only if the new version installs differently.
advanced.title: Advanced settings
advanced.intro_new: Settings most people never touch. Left alone, nothing changes: the application is created as usual.
advanced.intro_update: Filled with the settings the current application has in Intune. What you do not modify is kept as it is.
advanced.requirements_hint: Intune installs the application only on devices that meet them. An empty field means no requirement.
advanced.windows_unset: Not set on this application (left as it is)
advanced.restart_hint: The default follows the return code of the installer: 3010 and 1641 ask for a restart.
advanced.restart_return_code: Restart when the return code asks for it (default)
advanced.restart_allow: Leave it to the installer (restarts are not prevented)
advanced.restart_force: Always restart the device after the installation
advanced.max_run_time_hint: How long Intune waits for the installer to finish, from 1 to 1440. Empty: 60 minutes, the Intune default.
advanced.allow_uninstall: Allow uninstalling from the Company Portal (Available assignments)
detection.title: Detection rule
detection.text: How Intune knows this version is installed.
detection.keep_hint: The existing rules are copied. Version comparisons equal to the current version and MSI product codes are moved to the new version; anything else (a script, for example) stays as it is.
detection.version_ge: Version greater than or equal to
detection.check32: Look in the 32-bit locations on 64-bit Windows
mode.title: How to update
mode.label: Method
mode.supersede: New application that replaces the current one (recommended)
mode.inplace_hint: The installer of the existing application is replaced. Assignments do not change, there is no pilot phase and no going back.
mode.type_hint: Most installers upgrade in place: keep the first choice unless the vendor says otherwise.
mode.cleanup: Delete the oldest version from Intune once the new one is published, to keep two versions: {names}
done.title: Published
done.supersede: “{name}” was created in Intune and replaces the previous version.
done.cleanup_failed: The new version is published, but the oldest version could not be deleted: {names}.
done.delay: Intune can take a few minutes to show the application as ready.
warning.install_command_unchanged: The install command does not mention the setup file name, so it was kept as it is.
warning.detection_needs_review: The current application is detected by an MSI product code but the new file is not an MSI: fill in the detection rule.
warning.detection_exists_only: The detection rule only checks that a file or key exists: Intune will not see the difference between the old and the new version.
warning.detection_kept: The detection rules are too specific to be edited here: they are kept, check that they still match the new version.
error.session_expired: Your session has expired, please sign in again
error.not_configured: TENANT_ID and CLIENT_ID are not set
error.login_expired: The sign-in took too long, please try again
error.user_not_allowed: This account is not allowed to use this tool
error.url_required: Give a link or choose a file
error.url_scheme: The link must start with http:// or https://
error.download_http: The download was refused by the site
error.too_large: The file is larger than the allowed size
error.not_installer: The link does not return an MSI or EXE file (a web page, perhaps?)
error.bad_msi: The MSI file cannot be read
error.graph_forbidden: Your account does not have the rights for this action in Intune
error.not_win32: This is not a Win32 application
error.job_not_found: This task no longer exists, start again
error.job_not_ready: The file is not ready yet
error.group_picker_disabled: The group picker is not enabled
error.bad_product_code: The product code must look like {XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}
error.bad_detection: The detection rule is not valid
error.removal_no_name: Choose at least one program to remove
error.removal_bad_name: The list of programs is not valid
error.removal_bad_versions: The version rule is not valid
error.removal_bad_command: The uninstall command is not valid: one line, 1000 characters at most
error.detection_value: The detection rule needs a value
error.detection_file: The detection rule needs a folder and a file name
error.detection_registry: The detection rule needs a registry key
error.bad_run_as: An application installs as System or as User
error.advanced_number: A whole number greater than zero is expected (at most 1440 for the installation time)
error.bad_advanced: The advanced settings are not valid
error.config_unreadable: The file config/rollout.json cannot be read
error.no_production_groups: No production group is configured and there is no previous version to copy from
error.no_pilot_groups: Add at least one pilot group, or choose another assignment
error.login_unreachable: Microsoft sign-in cannot be reached: check TENANT_ID, CLIENT_ID and the Internet access of the server
footer.test_version_hint: Not yet validated on a real Intune tenant: try it on an unimportant application first.
error.config_not_writable: The config folder cannot be written, so pilot/production groups cannot be saved. On Linux, give it to the user set in docker-compose.yml: sudo chown -R 1000:1000 config
inventory.title: Software on the devices
inventory.search_device: Search by device, user or model
inventory.note: Read from the Intune inventory at {time}. Intune refreshes it about once a day, and it lists software whether or not Intune installed it.
inventory.no_software: Intune has not reported any software yet.
error.inventory_disabled: The device inventory is not enabled
removal.title: Software removals
removal.intro: Each rule removes one piece of software from the devices through Intune. Rules are kept in the local configuration folder (config/removals.json).
removal.none: No removal rule yet. Open a program in the device inventory to remove it.
removal.protected_notice: This software is protected: removing it would break device management, security or Windows. The tool refuses to remove it.
removal.warning: A removal cannot be undone: to bring the software back it has to be installed again. Start with a small group.
removal.exact_hint: Only software whose name is exactly one of these is removed. Add another name when the same program appears under several names.
removal.add_name: Add another name from the inventory
removal.versions_list_label: Versions to remove, separated by commas
removal.kind_machine_hint: The usual case (MSI or EXE installed by an administrator). Removed in the background, whoever is signed in.
removal.kind_user_hint: Installed without administrator rights. It is removed in the session of the user, so only while that user is signed in.
removal.kind_store_hint: Removed for every user of the device, along with the copy kept for future users.
removal.command_hint: Leave empty to start: MSI software and software that declares a silent uninstall are removed without it. If a device then fails with no silent method, add the vendor's command here. {UninstallString} is replaced by the uninstaller found on the device. The tool never tries switches at random.
removal.command_auto: Automatic (MSI, or the silent command the software declares)
removal.targets_hint: The removal only runs on devices where the software is found. Without a target, nothing happens yet.
removal.once_long: One-off: I end the rule when the software is gone
removal.permanent_long: Permanent: remove it again if it comes back
removal.preview: According to the inventory, {count} installation(s) would be removed.
removal.confirm_label: To confirm, type the name of the first software exactly
removal.remaining_value: {count} installation(s) according to the inventory, which Intune refreshes about once a day
removal.failed_hint: A failure usually means the software has no silent uninstall method on that device: add a command with “Change”. The details are in the device log IAFD-Remove-….log, in the Intune Management Extension log folder.
removal.results_unavailable: Intune did not return the per-device results. The rule still works; see the details in the Intune portal.
removal.open_portal: Open this application in the Intune portal
removal.finish_confirm: End the removal of “{name}”? Its application is deleted from Intune and no device is targeted any more. Software already removed stays removed.
removal.save_targets_hint: **Save targets** updates the assignment in Intune at once. A target taken out is no longer aimed at; software already removed stays removed.
removal.app_text: Intune uninstalls this application from the targets below, using its uninstall command. A target that was set to install it is switched to uninstall.
removal.app_targets_hint: The devices of these targets lose the application the next time they contact Intune. The other assignments are not changed.
removal.app_stop_hint: **Stop removing** takes these uninstall assignments away: no device is targeted any more, and the application is not put back where it was removed.
error.removal_protected: Protected software, the tool refuses to remove it:
error.removal_confirm: The name typed does not match the first software
error.removal_not_found: This removal rule no longer exists
error.replace_bad_install: The install command is not valid for a replacement: it must be on one line
replace.title: Devices that already have an older version
replace.enable: Install only on the devices where an older version is found
replace.hint: Intune then offers this application only to the devices that have one of these programs, in a version older than the one below. The names must be exactly those of the inventory.
replace.mode: How the old version is replaced
replace.upgrade: The installer upgrades over it (usual case)
replace.reinstall: Remove the old version first, then install
replace.upgrade_hint: Nothing else changes: the new installer does the upgrade.
replace.reinstall_hint: For programs that do not upgrade over an existing version. The old version is removed silently; if that fails, the new one is not installed.
replace.command_hint: Only needed when the old version is neither an MSI nor a program that declares a silent uninstall. {UninstallString} stands for its uninstaller.
error.remediations_disabled: Removal on a single device is not enabled
error.removal_not_editable: An on-demand removal cannot be changed: end it and start again from the device
removal.ondemand_text: Intune runs the removal on this device only, at its next check-in (usually within the hour when it is switched on). Remediations must have been enabled once in the Intune portal, with the Windows licence confirmed.
removal.confirm_label_one: To confirm, type the name of the software exactly
removal.on_demand_long: On demand, on the devices listed below
removal.on_demand_hint: To run it on another device, open that device in the inventory and choose “Remove here” with the same settings.
error.device_groups_disabled: Picking devices one by one is not enabled
error.removal_unknown_device: One of these devices no longer has the software according to the inventory: reload the page
removal.devices_text: Intune only targets groups. The devices you tick are added to a security group the tool creates for this rule in Microsoft Entra ID and deletes when the rule ends. Intune can take up to an hour to take a new group member into account.
removal.devices_load: Show the devices that have this software
removal.devices_none: According to the inventory, no device has this software any more.
removal.devices_missing: These devices have no object in Microsoft Entra ID and could not be added: {names}
